reviews.title: LÊ MINH VŨ · IELTS 49 · W07 · Đề 1
reviews.overall: Em đã viết đủ bốn đoạn và nhận ra chiều tăng của Argentina, chiều giảm của Australia cùng vị trí dẫn đầu của Thailand. Tuy nhiên, Overview nói Thailand tăng ở cuối kỳ, trái với bảng: nước này đạt đỉnh năm 2006 rồi giảm vào năm 2009. Argentina cũng đã vượt Australia ngay năm 2006, không phải đến năm 2009. Bài này em soát chưa kỹ: số đầu của Thailand bị chép sai, nhiều động từ và từ viết sai khiến câu khó hiểu. Cô yêu cầu em sửa dữ liệu và kiểm tra từng câu trước khi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em tách Argentina và Australia ở Detail 1, Thailand ở Detail 2; cách chia theo nước này phù hợp và mỗi Detail có ít nhất hai câu. Em có so sánh hai nước đầu, nhưng cần đặt đúng thời điểm Argentina vượt Australia và cho thấy Thailand tăng tới năm 2006 rồi giảm. Overview nên nêu các xu hướng chính thay vì gọi diễn biến của Thailand là một đợt tăng ở cuối kỳ.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given table illustrates how many cars produced in three coutries including Argentina, Australia and Thailand between 2003 and 2009

Overall, the number of cars made in Argentina was increased steadily, while an opposite trend was shown in Australia ; in addition, Thailand had some fluctuation , there was an upturn at the end of the period

To eleborate , the number of cars manufactured in Argentina was climbed steadily from 235,088 in 2003 and catched up with Australia in 2006 with the data pff 352,759 and overtook Australia with 466,089 in 2009. Conversely , the datas of Australia gradually losed from 452,163 in 2003 to 341,268 in 2006 , and finished at 245,624 then became the lowest data in 2009.

In terms of the final information , the number of cars made in Thailand had a huge increase from 735,855 to 1,162,356 reached the highest figure through the season over a three-year period , commencing from 2003. Then, there was decreased to 999,963 cars in 2009, but remanning the highest figure through out the
period. Finally, despite the fluctuation, the mumber of cars recognised to be made in Thailand had a noticable increase at the end of the period and the largest figures in comparison to the others data throughout the years.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The two line charts show how many male and female prisoners there were in a European country between 1911 and 2001.

Overall, the male prison population was higher than the female population throughout the period. The male total fell early on but rose sharply towards the end, whereas the female total reached its lowest point in 1941 and then fluctuated. In 2001, the female figure remained below its initial level.

The given line chart illustrates how female representation in parliament, expressed as a percentage, changed in Germany, Italy, France, the UK and Belgium between 2000 and 2012.

Overall, the proportion of female members of parliament rose in all five countries, although Germany changed only slightly and France rose before falling. France briefly had the highest figure in 2004, while Italy led by 2012. The UK started at the lowest level and ended level with Belgium.

In 2000, about 33% of members of parliament in Germany were women, with a subsequent slight rise to 37% in 2012. By comparison, the figure for Italy climbed more markedly from roughly 26% to 39% over the same period, overtaking that for Germany by the end.

Regarding the remaining countries, the proportion in France rose from around 25% in 2000 to a peak of 37% in 2004 before falling to approximately 31% in 2012. Belgium's figure increased from about 17% to 28% by 2004 and then remained close to that level. Finally, the UK recorded just 3% in 2000, but its figure reached about 28% in 2012, matching that for Belgium.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given pie graphs illustrate the reasons of how students made choices to adopt a particular university in the UK in one decades.

Overall, suitable degree courses were increased slightly marking the most popular reason in both years, while good sports and social activities became less important due to the noticeable fall. In addition, the percentages for distance, and educantional quality reasons were increased, whereas the others experienced a decline.

To elaborate, the proportion of students who decided to go to the university because of suitable degree courses rose slightly from 35% in 1997 to 37% in 2007, but remained the highest option of students . Similarly , the figures for quality of teaching increased from 15% to 18%. Proximity to the parental home also experienced a considerable increase , rising from 10% to 22% over the same period.

In terms of the remained reasons of choosing university , the percentage of students who considered the quality of resources important fell from 21% in 1997 to 17% in 2007 .Also of note is that the figures for good sports and social activities dropped significantly from 19% to just 6%, marking the lowest figure at the end of the period

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The pie charts show how the proportions of students selecting a particular university in the UK for five different reasons changed between 1997 and 2007.

Overall, the percentage choosing the university for suitable degree courses remained the highest in both years, rising slightly. Proximity to parental home and teaching quality also became more common reasons, whereas the proportions citing resources and sports and social activities declined. By 2007, the last of these was the least common reason.

To elaborate, in 1997, 35% of students chose the university because it offered suitable degree courses, with a slight rise to 37% in 2007. The percentage citing proximity to parental home grew more markedly from 10% to 22%, the largest increase among the five reasons. Similarly, the figure for quality of teaching went up from 15% to 18%.

Regarding the two declining reasons, the proportion of students choosing the university for its quality of resources fell from 21% to 17%. That for good sports and social activities dropped much more sharply, from 19% to 6%, making it the smallest category in 2007.

Overall, the amount of citizens aged 65 and above in all three countries projected to increase over the period examined.Also of note is that, Germany also has the highest percentages, while the UK remaining the lowest figures.

In terms of the UK,in 1988, an insignificant 14.25% people of 65 years old and over increased slightly to 14.80% in 2000,after which, a prediction of a significant rise to 20,45% in 2030, despite that, its figures stay the lowest of the entire chart.The opposite position is true in Germany,it is likely to maintain the country with the highest proportion of elderly people.

The table compares the shares of people aged 65 and above in Canada, Germany and the UK in 1988 and 2000, together with projections for 2030.

Overall, the proportion of older residents rose in each country between 1988 and 2000 and is expected to increase further by 2030. Germany records the highest figures in all three years, while the UK has the lowest; Canada remains between them.

In 1988, 16.45% of Canada's population was aged 65 or above, compared with 20.35% in Germany. These figures rose to 20.65% and 25.53%, respectively, in 2000. Canada's share is projected to reach 26.35% by 2030, while Germany's is expected to increase to 30.65%. Germany is thus forecast to retain its lead.

The UK had the smallest share of older residents, at 14.25% in 1988. This figure increased only slightly to 14.80% in 2000, a rise of 0.55 percentage points. A more pronounced increase to 20.45% is predicted for 2030, although the UK is expected to remain below Canada and Germany.
